novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism/measurement hypothesis: a "separable, additive internal 'mention flag'" that transfers "ACROSS frames (quotation, attribution, hypothetical, negation)" and causally controls whether framed content is treated as asserted. Searches for "LLM use-mention representation hidden states," "assertion status quotation negation linear probe," "belief attribution representation steering," and "prompt injection instruction data role geometry" found the closest precedents in Language Models Represent Beliefs of Self and Others (2024), The Instruction Hierarchy (2024), StruQ (2024), and Probing for Knowledge Attribution (2026), but these respectively concern belief-holder/source representations, instruction priority, or context-source attribution rather than one proposition-level status variable shared across semantic frames. Moving from those works to a cross-frame, additively composing use-versus-mention signal requires a new core relationship rather than a direct transfer, although the individual probing and steering methods are standard, supporting high novelty within an established mechanistic-interpretability framework rather than paradigm-level novelty.
